security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives: markdown examples with placeholder URLs, task construction, and inline-code file paths. One semantic issue remains: the async database example builds SQL with f-strings around user_id, which can teach unsafe query construction. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Insecure SQL interpolation in async database example
remediation.suggestion: Replace f-string SQL examples with parameterized query placeholders and describe safe query binding.

content.value_statement: Async Python code can fail through blocking calls, weak cancellation, or uncontrolled concurrency. This skill gives practical asyncio patterns for reliable services, APIs, scrapers, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Explains asyncio basics, coroutines, tasks, futures, async context managers, and async iterators.
Shows patterns for gather, task creation, timeouts, semaphores, queues, locks, and rate limiting.
Provides examples for aiohttp web scraping, async database access, WebSocket handling, and connection pooling.
Covers testing async functions with pytest-asyncio and timeout assertions.
Highlights common pitfalls like missing await, blocking the event loop, and weak cancellation handling.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a runnable package or library.
It assumes Python 3.7 or newer and an asyncio-compatible runtime.
It does not replace framework-specific security review for production services.
Database and network examples are simplified and need production hardening, including parameterized queries.

use_cases.title: Build Async APIs
use_cases.description: Design request handlers, background tasks, and timeout rules for non-blocking Python services.

use_cases.title: Process I/O Workloads
use_cases.description: Use queues, semaphores, batching, and connection pools for concurrent network or database tasks.

use_cases.title: Test Async Behavior
use_cases.description: Create async tests that cover successful work, failures, timeouts, and cancellation paths.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Async Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python workflow and tell me whether asyncio is appropriate. Separate I/O-bound tasks from CPU-bound tasks and note runtime constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Blocking I/O
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this synchronous I/O workflow into an asyncio design. Include tasks, awaits, timeouts, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Concurrency Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an async processing pipeline for these inputs. Add queue limits, semaphores, cancellation rules, and retry boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Async Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async Python service for event loop blocking, leaked tasks, missing awaits, weak cancellation, and missing tests. Prioritize risks.

output_examples.input: A synchronous service calls three APIs before responding.
output: Recommended pattern: create bounded concurrent tasks with shared timeout budgets.
Add per-request error handling so one failed call does not hide other results.
Test timeout and cancellation paths with async-aware tests.

output_examples.input: A scraper starts hundreds of requests at once.
output: Recommended pattern: use semaphores and connection pooling to cap active requests.
Add backpressure so new work waits when the queue is full.
Record failures separately from successful responses for retry decisions.
Recommended checks: missing await, blocking calls, and tasks that ignore cancellation.
Add explicit timeout assertions and cleanup checks.
Verify that background tasks finish before the test ends.

best_practices: Define timeouts, cancellation behavior, and concurrency limits before adding new async tasks.
Use async-native I/O libraries and parameterized database queries; offload blocking work only when needed.
Test success, failure, timeout, and cancellation paths with async-aware test tools.
anti_patterns: Do not use asyncio for CPU-bound work unless you offload it to a process or thread pool.
Do not create unbounded tasks without rate limits, queue limits, or backpressure.
Do not call blocking functions inside async code unless they run outside the event loop.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design async Python APIs, services, scrapers, queues, and tests that use asyncio patterns.

faq.question: Does it execute network requests?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance. Network URLs appear only inside examples.

faq.question: Which Python versions fit these patterns?
faq.answer: The examples target modern asyncio usage, especially Python 3.7 and newer.

faq.question: Can I use it with FastAPI or aiohttp?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance fits async frameworks that run on Python event loops.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready database code?
faq.answer: No. Treat database examples as simplified patterns and use parameterized queries in production.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CPU-heavy workloads?
faq.answer: Not by itself. CPU-heavy work usually needs multiprocessing, native extensions, or executor offloading.
